### A Well-Chosen Word
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-february-27-2023.html
Passage: Proverbs 25:11
Points:
- Spoken words give shape and direction to internal thoughts and feelings.
- A well-timed word spoken in need can instantly revive hope and dissolve self-doubt.
- Careless speech carries immense destructive power to crush the human spirit.
- Though physical monuments and worldly empires crumble over time, fitly spoken words endure.

### Bouncing Back
Author: Kelly McFadden
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-mar-17-2009-11600945.html
Passage: Proverbs 25:11
Points:
- Wise, timely counsel can transform our mindset in the midst of bitter disappointment.
- What happens in life matters far less than how we choose to respond to our circumstances.
- Daily adversity forces a choice between nursing resentment and pursuing patient growth.
- People watch how believers respond to setbacks, making resilience an essential Christian witness.

### Walls of Protection
Author: Leading The Way
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-week-of-october-20-11583128.html
Passage: Proverbs 25:28
Points:
- Ancient city walls provided vital defense, and their destruction left inhabitants completely vulnerable.
- A person who lacks self-control is spiritually exposed to the enemy's destructive schemes.
- Unrestrained passions allow sins such as rage, jealousy, and gossip to overrun the heart.
- Confessing sin and turning to God restores divine walls of protection around our lives.

### My First Tattoo
Author: Noelle Dey
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/my-first-tattoo-encouragement-caf-october-1-2015.html
Passage: Proverbs 25:28
Points:
- Physical exhaustion and stress often reveal a failure to maintain biblical self-control.
- Failing to set boundaries and say no allows unnecessary burdens to break down our health.
- When personal self-control fails, other spiritual virtues like patience and gentleness decline as well.
- Believers must evaluate their commitments to ensure they only carry tasks authored by God.
